research: Line: slate St. John's -28.5; archive open -27.5, close -28.5. Slate and close agree, so the market settled right on this number (slate archive) - neutral.
Total moved 156.5 -> 158.5 at the close (slate archive), so the market expected a bit more scoring, which slightly favors a bigger margin - mild St. John's.
Rick Pitino is 20-0 at Carnesecca Arena with an average 24.1-point margin, per the school (Predictem, Nov 11). That average is a few points under -28.5 - mild Colgate.
St. John's beat Iona 104-65 and Monmouth by 15; Pitino called the Monmouth game 'mediocre' after a strong first 10 minutes (Predictem, Nov 11). Two very different margins - neutral.

[angle] The St. John's press has produced 23 steals and 37 forced turnovers worth 47 points in two games (Predictem, Nov 11). Colgate's answer is ball security at about 9.5 turnovers a game. That is the key matchup, and Colgate's low turnover rate helps it - mild Colgate.

Colgate is 0-2: it lost to Washington by 14 after leading part of the first half, and lost 77-74 at Drexel after blowing an 11-point second-half lead (Predictem, Nov 11). It is competitive but not closing games - Colgate can score.
Andrew Alekseyenko (last year's Patriot League Rookie of the Year) averages 22.5 points and 12.5 rebounds and is 7-of-11 from three; Sam Wright scored 21 at Drexel (Predictem, Nov 11) - Colgate.
[angle] Colgate lost its top scorer and assist man, Jalen Cox, to USC in the transfer portal (Predictem, Nov 11), which weakens its handling against a press - St. John's.

[angle] Pitino said 'Colgate is a team that will take 40 3s if they have to' (Predictem, Nov 11). A three-heavy underdog brings variance both ways: a cold night means a blowout, a hot one means a cover - neutral.

St. John's depth: Quinn Ellis has 18 assists to 2 turnovers, Baylor transfer Tounde Yessoufou scored 23 vs Iona, Keyshawn Hall averages 19.5 and Ian Jackson is 6-of-13 from three (Predictem, Nov 11) - St. John's.
Schedule: St. John's plays Syracuse at MSG three days later (Predictem, Nov 11), a possible look-ahead or reason to rest starters late - mild Colgate.
Predictem's model has St. John's by about 23 and lists Colgate +28.5 as only 'a lean' (Predictem, Nov 11). Preview picks are already priced - tiebreaker at most.
games.reasoning: The close sits right at the slate's 28.5, and the strongest finding is Pitino's 24-point average home margin against a Colgate team that protects the ball, but that is priced. The press-versus-ball-security matchup is the most interesting angle, offset by losing Cox. No read on a 25+ college line, so pass; Colgate is the forced side on ball security alone.

research: Line: slate Michigan -3.5; archive open -4.5, close -2.5. The market moved two points toward Marquette, and against the close the slate's +3.5 is a better number than the market's final price - Marquette at the slate number, but the move is priced.
Total moved up from 153.5 to 157.5 (slate archive).
Barttorvik ranks Michigan 21st and Marquette 23rd overall; Marquette's defense is 13th to Michigan's 18th (Predictem, Nov 11). The teams are nearly even, so the home edge is about the line - neutral.
[angle] Michigan is in a coaching transition: Dusty May left for the Dallas Mavericks and Mike Boynton Jr. took over the defending champions (Predictem, Nov 11) - mild Marquette.

Michigan's guards are cold: they shot 23% from three as a team, Cadeau is 1-of-9, Gayle has no threes in two games, and they went 7-of-34 from three vs Oakland (Covers, Nov 11; Predictem, Nov 11). That is a two-game sample from a 38% shooter, which suggests regression at home - Michigan.
Trey McKenney averages 19.5 points and is 7-of-15 from three, with all 22 of his points vs UConn after halftime; J.P. Estrella averages 17.0 points and 10.5 rebounds (Predictem, Nov 11) - Michigan.
[angle] Michigan's bigs are in foul trouble: Estrella fouled out of the opener in 21 minutes and had four more fouls vs UConn, and Thiam had four in 15 minutes (Predictem, Nov 11) - Marquette.

Marquette's defense held Detroit Mercy and Mercyhurst to 37.5 points a game on 25.6% shooting and 9-of-55 from three, and forces turnovers on 28.1% of possessions (Predictem, Nov 11; Covers, Nov 11). Those were weak opponents, so treat the numbers as inflated - mild Marquette.
[angle] This is Marquette's first road game and first ranked opponent. It went 12-20 last season and 2-10 on the road, and hasn't won in Ann Arbor since 1954 (Predictem, Nov 11) - mild Michigan.

Michigan lost 85-77 to UConn in Boston, with 11 first-half turnovers, and is trying to avoid its first two-game losing streak since 2024-25 (Predictem; Covers, Nov 11). Bounce-back motivation at home - mild Michigan.
Marquette has covered 10 of its last 13 games and gone Under in 10 of 13 (Covers, Nov 11) - ATS records are priced, mild Marquette at most.
Both Covers (Marquette +3.5, combo with Under) and Predictem (Marquette +3.5, projecting 78-76) take Marquette (Nov 11). Public-facing previews on one side line up with the move to -2.5 - priced.
games.reasoning: Two even teams by Torvik, a close of -2.5, and a projection of Michigan by about 3 put this inside the pass band. The coaching change and foul trouble favor Marquette, and Michigan's likely shooting regression at home favors Michigan. The market already moved toward Marquette, so there is nothing unpriced. Forced Michigan on the shooting regression against a defense whose numbers came against weak opponents.

Writer's pick Jacksonville State +36.5 (Predictem, Nov 11) - preview picks are priced, tiebreaker only.
Only about 10 solid facts were found for this game; no injury news for either side.
games.reasoning: The slate's 36.5 sits 3 points above the 33.5 close, a data flag, so no case can rest on either number. Houston's elite defense against a sloppy Jacksonville State is real but priced in a 30+ line. Pass on a 25+ college line; forced Jacksonville State only because the slate number is above the close.

[angle] Arkansas comes home off a 91-72 loss at Virginia, which John Calipari called 'a punch in the mouth' (Predictem, Nov 11). A motivated response at home against a weak opponent - mild Arkansas.
Arkansas beat Arkansas-Pine Bluff by 45 in its opener, scoring 106 (Predictem, Nov 11) - mild Arkansas.
Arkansas blocks 8.5 shots a game, and Billy Richmond III and Maper Maker each had three vs Virginia (Predictem, Nov 11). That is a problem for a 33%-shooting team - Arkansas.

Freshman Jordan Smith Jr. averages 19.5 points for Arkansas (Predictem, Nov 11) - Arkansas.

games.reasoning: Robert Morris's offense (52.5 ppg, 19.5 turnovers) against Arkansas's shot-blocking is the clearest mismatch, but 'the underdog can't score' is priced and has lost before. The slate's -31.5 is 2 points above the -29.5 close. No read on a 25+ line, so pass. Forced Arkansas on the matchup and Calipari's short rotation.
